A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spacetime information-geometry framework. Their complete main texts, equations, Table 1, eight figures and appendices are readable and can be matched across formatting changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture trajectory experiments, ImageNet image-similarity analyses and alanine-dipeptide transition-path results in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original toy and image experiments and reports revised molecular transition-path results in Table 1, with settings in Appendix G.3.

M1.justification: The Fisher-Rao spacetime construction, energy objective, denoiser training and annealed-Langevin procedure are retained. New Algorithms 2–4 document the existing curve evaluation, geodesic optimization and DiffED computation; they do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same one-dimensional Gaussian mixture, ImageNet-512 images and alanine-dipeptide dihedral-angle landscape. Image interpolation, sampling-trajectory comparison, transition-path generation and constrained transitions retain the same coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain PF-ODE trajectories; LPIPS, SSIM and Euclidean image distances; and fixed-length MCMC, variable-length MCMC and Doob's Lagrangian. Holdijk et al. and Raja et al. remain discussed but excluded from the reported transition-path comparison.

E3.justification: For molecular sampling, v2 Appendix F.3 specifies endpoint log-SNR 7, 512 geodesic points and Langevin step size 0.0001; v3 Appendix G.3 specifies 4, 128 and 0.0004, respectively. The timing example changes from 8 to 1,000 parallel paths, although both main comparisons already report 1,000 paths. These are localized reported setting revisions.

E4.justification: The low-variance and region-avoidance demonstrations in Section 6.4, qualitative transition-path comparison and image-similarity examples are retained. Their figures are unchanged, and no new ablation, sensitivity, robustness or error analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean MaxEnergy with accompanying ± values for 1,000 paths, without adding uncertainty definitions, seed information or significance tests. The changed parallel-generation batch concerns the sampling procedure, not an established increase in repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the proposed method's MaxEnergy of 37.66 ± 0.61 with 37.36 ± 0.60 under revised settings. Reported generation cost rises from 128K to 16M evaluations, with the additional 16M training-data cost retained. This substantially changes the computational advantage, although baseline scores and the MaxEnergy ranking remain unchanged. Appendix timings also change under different discretization and batch sizes, so they do not establish same-setting speedups.

T1.justification: Corollary C.1 expands from continuous energy alone to include continuous curve length and explicit discrete energy and length approximations, with their derivation in v3 Equations 42–45. The principal pullback-collapse, exponential-family and KL results remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: pullback degeneracy, Fisher-Rao spacetime geometry, tractable geodesics, DiffED and molecular transition-path applications. Neither the scope nor the scientific strength of these central claims changes.

C2.justification: The edit-distance interpretation, distinction from perceptual similarity, baseline-collapse discussion and limitations concerning nearly clean endpoints and slow DiffED computation are retained. Section 6.3 also retains its computational-efficiency interpretation despite the revised evaluation counts.

D1.justification: v3 adds explicit pseudocode for curve evaluation, geodesic estimation and DiffED, plus a reproducibility statement saying source code accompanies the submission. Appendix G.3 provides clearer per-path and total sampling-cost accounting and revised timing information. The existing public code reference and other implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same, including distinctions from projected latent geometries, other Fisher-Rao formulations and Wasserstein approaches. The expanded derivation references the already-cited Arvanitidis et al. work without changing the paper's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds a pseudocode appendix and reproducibility statement, expands the Corollary C.1 exposition and makes limited terminology edits. The main section order and nearly all narrative are retained; subsequent appendices are renumbered.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes the title and author block, margins, figure sizing and display placement. Figure 6 moves before Table 1, Figures 7 and 8 are relocated, and three algorithm displays are added. All eight figure images and Table 1's row-and-column structure are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through explicit algorithms and length-discretization derivations, and brings Table 1's sampling cost much closer to the appendix's per-path accounting. The benefit is limited: the revised score uses changed settings, and Section 6.3 still claims several orders of magnitude fewer evaluations despite 16M versus 1.29B supporting only about an 81-fold reduction before training-data cost.
